Environmental economics

Environmental economics studies how economic decisions affect environmental resources and how policy can address environmental problems. Pollution and resource depletion often create costs that are not fully reflected in market prices.

The field therefore examines instruments such as taxes, regulation, property rights, and markets for environmental services. It also considers how environmental benefits and costs can be measured and valued.
